title: Data policies (DLP) for Copilot Studio agents
summary: Hold: the permissions guidance omits the System Administrator requirement for environments with Dataverse, and the default-group explanation omits the exception for nonblockable connectors. The page also incorrectly implies that fixing an agent requires changing its policy, and makes unsupported exclusions about which controls can affect connectors and MCP tools.

claims.where: What it is; summary
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies govern which connectors apps, flows and Copilot Studio agents can use together.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Microsoft also calls a data policy a data loss prevention (DLP) policy.
claims.quote: Endpoint filtering rules are evaluated in order, based on the allow and deny patterns configured in the data loss prevention (DLP) policy.

claims.where: What it is; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: Data policies classify connectors into Business, Non-Business and Blocked data groups.
claims.quote: The three data groups are the Business data group, the Non-Business data group, and the Blocked data group.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Connectors in different data groups cannot share data.
claims.quote: You can't share data among connectors that are located in different groups.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: An app or flow cannot combine SharePoint in Business with Gmail in Non-Business.
claims.quote: if you place SharePoint and Salesforce connectors in the Business group and you place Gmail in the Non-Business group, makers can't create an app or flow that uses both the SharePoint and Gmail connectors.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: A connector classified as Blocked cannot be used where the policy applies.
claims.quote: Blocked connectors can't be used where this policy is applied.

claims.quote: Since early 2025, data policy enforcement is in effect for all tenants, as announced in the message center alert MC973179: Copilot Studio - Upcoming updates to data loss prevention enforcement.

claims.where: What it is; changes
claims.claim: Since March 2025, agents cannot be exempted from data policy enforcement.
claims.quote: Since March 2025, agents can't be exempted from data policy enforcement. It's no longer possible to exempt agents with a PowerShell command.

claims.where: What it is

claims.quote: Virtual connectors are connectors that appear in data policies for administrators to control, but they're not based on a RESTful API.

claims.where: Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: A tenant-scoped policy applies to all agents in all environments across the tenant.
claims.quote: Policies with a tenant scope apply to all agents in all environments across the tenant.
claims.fix: Qualify the sentence and controls[0].note: 'A policy configured with Add all environments applies across the tenant. Tenant-level policies can also include or exclude selected environments.' The cited agent page supports the original wording, but https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss explicitly says tenant-level policies can include or exclude specific environments.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Connectors introduced after 2019, including unauthenticated chat and Direct Line, are likely to be in the default Non-business group.
claims.quote: Connectors introduced after 2019, such as Chat without Microsoft Entra ID authentication in Copilot Studio or Direct Line channels in Copilot Studio, are likely to be part of the default "Non-business" group.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft says many organisations automatically block connectors in the Non-business group.
claims.quote: In many organizations, connectors in the "Non-business" group are automatically blocked.

claims.where: Why it matters
claims.claim: Microsoft warns that blocking new connectors by default can cause production outages, including Direct Line or unauthenticated website agents.
claims.quote: Misaligned configurations, such as data policies blocking new connectors by default, could result in production outages. For example, essential features like Direct Line or unauthenticated agent deployments on websites might be unexpectedly blocked.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: At the time of writing, the data policy documentation states no licence or charge specific to data policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Platform data policies DLP license licensing additional cost charge; "Power Platform" "data policies" "licensing" "cost". Opened Data policies, Manage data policies and Configure data policies for agents; no separate policy licence or charge stated.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Assign connectors Class column indicates whether connector usage requires a Premium licence.
claims.quote: Class | Indicates whether connector usage requires a Premium license or is it included in the Built-in/Standard license for Power Platform.

claims.where: Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Microsoft says connectors requiring licensing not included in the user's licence are not visible to that user.
claims.quote: Some connectors require specific licensing, and if your license doesn't include them, you can't see them.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Creating a policy requires the tenant admin or Environment Admin role, without a Dataverse qualification.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.
claims.fix: Replace the role sentence in Cost and licensing and the role wording in controls[0].note and its rendered row with: 'Tenant-level policies require Power Platform Administrator permissions. For environment-level policies, you need Environment Admin permissions, or the System Administrator role for environments with a Dataverse database.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: The initial default group for new connectors is Non-Business.
claims.quote: Initially, the Non-Business group is the default group for new connectors and all services.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: New connectors enter the policy's default group and are blocked when that default is blocked, without exception.
claims.quote: If Microsoft adds any new connectors that can't be blocked and you set the default group for the data policy as Blocked, these connectors are automatically marked as Non-Business instead of Blocked.
claims.fix: Replace the first sentence with: 'New connectors normally enter the policy's default group, initially Non-Business; new nonblockable connectors enter Non-Business even if the default is Blocked.' In the following sentence, replace 'A policy that blocks that group blocks newly introduced connectors' with 'A Blocked default group blocks newly introduced blockable connectors'. Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/dlp-connector-classification.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Default group
claims.claim: Published agents depending on newly blocked connectors show errors until the policy changes.
claims.quote: The admin can check the data policy violations and update the policies or the agent configuration as needed.
claims.fix: Replace 'published agents that depend on them show errors until the policy changes' with 'published agents that violate a policy show errors until the policy or agent configuration is corrected'. The source explicitly permits correcting the agent, not just changing policy.
